topics.title: About the poet and the poem

concepts.learning_objective: Recall key facts about John Keats as a British Romantic poet.
Explain the Greek legend of Endymion from which the poem is taken.
Explain why the poet calls a thing of beauty a joy forever whose loveliness increases.
Interpret the images of the quiet bower and the sleep full of sweet dreams.
Identify the things the poet lists as causes of suffering and gloom.
Interpret the image of wreathing a flowery band that binds us to the earth.
Explain how some shape of beauty moves away the pall from our dark spirits.
List and interpret the objects of nature the poet calls things of beauty.
Use the meanings of words such as rills, brake and covert to read the nature images.

topics.title: The mighty dead, lovely tales and the endless fountain

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why grandeur is associated with the mighty dead and lovely tales.
Interpret the image of an endless fountain of immortal drink from heaven's brink.
Analyse the poem's rhyming couplets and balanced sentence structure.
